neighbours.label: The adjective suffix -able/-ible (as a split piece like wash|able or inside a whole-word token like ' printable'), meaning 'can be X-ed', vs the same base verb or the word 'able' without the suffix
fire: The camping set comes with a foldable table and two chairs.
After filtering, the river water was finally drinkable.
Please pack the breakable dishes in extra newspaper.
The museum offers downloadable audio guides for every room.
The software stores every report in a searchable archive.
His handwriting is barely readable after a long day.
We bought a portable heater for the drafty garage.
Even a tiny crack became visible under the lamp.
quiet: The camping set comes with a table that folds and two chairs.
After filtering, we could finally drink the river water.
Please pack the dishes that might break in extra newspaper.
The museum lets you download audio guides for every room.
The software stores every report so that you can search it.
He was barely able to write after a long day.
We bought a small heater and a long cable for the garage.
Even a tiny crack showed up under the lamp.

predictions: -able/-ible adjectives 0.2-0.6; the same base verbs in 'can be X-ed' phrasing, 'able to', and -able spellings that are not the suffix (table, cable) under 0.1.
notes: Card: 'able' x12 plus ' adjustable', ' clickable', 'ible', 'IBLE'. Probe: wash|able 0.420, ' Printable' 0.586, repro|ducible 0.334, ' adjustable' 0.265, ' edible' 0.215, ' acceptable' 0.192; ' able' in 'was able to' 0.028, ' cable' 0.022. So the pole tracks the suffix, not the letters.
